stem.en: Tiger and lion share the genus Panthera. What does this tell you about their family?

text.en: They can be in two families, as genus and family are unrelated.

feedback.en: A genus sits inside a family, so the two levels are linked.

text.en: They share a family, as a genus sits inside one family.

feedback.en: Right. Every lower group is a part of the group above it, so both are in Felidae.

text.en: Sharing a genus can never tell us anything about family.

feedback.en: It tells us the family, and also every level above the family.

text.en: They must be one species, so the family does not matter.

feedback.en: Sharing a genus does not make them one species: they are Panthera tigris and Panthera leo.

explanation.en: Every lower group is a part of the group above it. Panthera sits inside the family Felidae, so the tiger and the lion both belong to Felidae, and to every larger group above it.

hints.en: Think of each group as sitting inside the one above it.
